newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says will mediate in Angola dispute.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says will mediate in Angola dispute.

text.p: South Africa will mediate in efforts to settle the status of former rebel leader Jonas Savimbi in Angola's government of national unity, state radio reported on Wednesday.
The radio quoted South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki as saying the Pretoria government would act as a go-between in the continuing political dispute in Angola.
It did not give further details.
Savimbi led a delegation of his UNITA movement to South Africa's Transkei region for a two-day round of talks with President Nelson Mandela, who was holidaying in the area.
Savimbi and President Jose Eduardo dos Santos are trying to put the new government together under a 1994 peace plan that ended two decades of civil war. Progress has been slow.
The two rivals agreed last month to form a government of national reconciliation on January 23 in a landmark move on the country's path to peace.

UNITA has proposed that Savimbi become leader of Angola's official opposition in parliament, rather than take up a vice presidential position offered by the ruling MPLA, which he has already rejected.
